review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for uses of gameAdd_iff, gameAdd_mk_iff, gameAdd_mk'_iff and gameAdd_swap_swap. They are only used inside this file. The single @[simp] lemma, Prod.gameAdd_swap_swap, looks fine. I made no loop claims and could not run Lean. The finding is a moderate-confidence orientation and normal-form concern about Sym2.gameAdd_iff, based on reading the statement and its one use. I did not read the Sym2 simp set or `Function.onFun` in detail to confirm exactly how the simpa at line 201 behaves.

findings.excerpt: GameAdd rα s(x.1, x.2) s(y.1, y.2) ↔ Prod.GameAdd rα rα x y ∨ Prod.GameAdd rα rα x.swap y
findings.problem: The statement's left side is written `s(x.1, x.2)`, which is `Sym2.mk (x.1, x.2)`. That is not in simp normal form, because the simp lemma `Prod.mk.eta` rewrites `(x.1, x.2)` to `x`. So the lemma could never be a useful `@[simp]` rule or a reliable rewrite rule: a `simp` call would first turn the term into `Sym2.mk x` and the lemma would no longer match. The only use, at line 201, goes through this fragile path: `simpa [← Sym2.gameAdd_iff]` rewrites right to left, and the result then has to line up with `hr.sym2_gameAdd.onFun` after simp has normalised the pair projections. The reader can't tell whether that works by design or by accident. The mk-form `gameAdd_mk'_iff` is stated by `Iff.rfl`, but it has no simp attribute and no canonical orientation either.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma on `Sym2.mk` directly: `GameAdd rα (Sym2.mk x) (Sym2.mk y) ↔ Prod.GameAdd rα rα x y ∨ Prod.GameAdd rα rα x.swap y`. The proof stays `rfl` after `rintro ⟨_, _⟩ ⟨_, _⟩`. This is the normal form that simp reaches, so it can be used directly. Then replace the `simpa [← Sym2.gameAdd_iff] using ...` at line 201 by a direct term, such as `Sym2.gameAdd_iff.symm`-based, or `simpa only [← Sym2.gameAdd_iff]`. That avoids relying on the full default simp set to reconcile the two forms.
findings.benefit: The unfolding lemma for `Sym2.GameAdd` is stated in the form simp produces, so the lemma can be used as a `simp`/`rw` rule on `Sym2.mk x` terms. The recursion proof no longer depends on the default simp set undoing `Prod.mk.eta` and `Sym2.mk`-projection mismatches.
